output.title: Spot free-tier limits before they interrupt work
output.body:
If you run a 1–10-person business and use free-tier tools, one useful workflow decision is simple: do you know the limit before the tool stops being useful? That applies to SaaS plans, APIs, email tools, or any service that quietly turns convenience into a bill or a block.

The question to ask is not “Can this tool do the job?” It is “Do I know the quota, and do I check usage before the limit is hit?” If the answer is no, you are leaving the timing to the vendor. That is rarely the best control surface.

A practical next step is to pick one tool in your stack and write down three things: the free limit, where usage is visible, and what reminder will make you look at it. For some tools, a weekly calendar check is enough. For faster-moving usage, a vendor alert email is better. Boring is fine here.

Why it matters: an unexpected limit can interrupt a workflow or force an unplanned upgrade while you are still deciding whether the process is worth automating. Early spotting does not make that decision for you, but it keeps it human and deliberate.

Start with one tool, one limit, and one check point.
